Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Discussed success criteria for POC, clarified TTFT vs TPOT, set p95/p99 targets for inference, agreed measurement plan and artifacts to share. Next: share scripts/traces and schedule baseline + stress benchmarks.
---
00:00 Jordan: All right good morning everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i have Priya our SE with me; quick roll call?
00:07 Samir: Hey Samir here, ... Samir Patel, Head of ML at Acme.
00:12 Lynn: Lynn, platform eng, hello.
00:17 Diego: Diego - SRE.
00:20 Priya: Great, thanks. Goal for today's call is to scope the POC -- specifically latency and throughput SLOs, workload sizing and a measurement plan.
01:02 Jordan: High level that Redwood can run hosted or dedicated for the POC, we typically recommend dedicated for tight p99s but hosted is faster to start; want to understand your success criteria.
02:10 Samir: Success criteria first - for us it's user-facing latency and availability. We have two primary use cases: interactive agent queries (real-time answer generation, short prompt -> single-turn) and document summarization batch jobs (multi-turn, longer context). For interactive we need low tail latency. For batch we care throughput.
03:00 Priya: Okay got it. Quick definitions i want to make sure we align on: TTFT - time to first token, the initial generation latency; TPOT - time per token (or per-token throughput) across a response. folks sometimes call it T-T-F-T and T-pot in notes, so just clarifying.
03:30 Diego: yes that matches our internal terms, we also look at p95 and p99 for both.
04:05 Lynn: our target for interactive flows is p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms for first token, and for sustained responses p95 per-token ~ 50ms. Is that realistic?
04:35 Priya: those are aggressive for larger models; depends on model size and quantization. On our Dedicated infra we can hit p95 TTFT ~200-350ms for optimized 7B/13B models with batched KV cache; for 70B it will be higher. There's also tradeoffs when you enable batching - improves TPOT but might add TTFT.
05:12 Jordan: to translate to a POC we'd clarify the representative model family (they mentioned closed-world open models earlier) and the sequence lengths. Samir, what model sizes do you plan to evaluate?
05:35 Samir: For POC we want to test a 13B for interactive and a 33B-ish for summarization. We can also try 7B as a baseline. We'll provide prompt templates and a 48h trace of production traffic.
06:05 Priya: Great. For benchmarking we'll run two scenarios: 1) baseline latency run - single-client steady-rate with concurrency low to measure TTFT under minimal batching; 2) throughput/stress run - ramp to desired RPS to evaluate TPOT and p99 under load. We'll also run warm vs cold cache experiments to see KV cache effects.
06:45 Diego: what's your definition of warm vs cold? We saw variance in p99s when cache miss rate is high.
07:00 Priya: Warm = KV cache populated by previous requests for the same session/prefix, cold = empty KV cache causing full context recompute. We'll capture both in runs.
07:20 Lynn: timeline - we want initial results within two weeks.
07:35 Jordan: workable. We'll draft benchmark plan and scripts today and get them over; customer provides traces and prompt set. Plan to run baseline the week of Feb 23.
08:10 Samir: On metrics, we want p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT, plus aggregate throughput (requests per second), tokens per second, and overall error rates and variant failures. Also breakdown of time in kernel vs queueing.
08:55 Priya: We'll capture token-level timing and queue latency from the runtime; Redwood Console can export per-route traces. We'll include guidance how to instrument. Note sometimes console names the metrics differently, e.g., "first_token_ms" or "time_to_first" in older exports.
09:25 Diego: Is CPU or network sometimes the dominant variable?
09:32 Priya: On Dedicated GPU infra network can matter if model shards or KV cache go over network, but usually GPU compute and kernel selection dominate. We will record GPU utilization, host CPU, and network IO during runs.
10:05 Jordan: Security check - you'll need SOC2 docs and KMS integration notes?
10:12 Lynn: Yes, share SOC2 + encryption-at-rest details, and we need to know if logs will leave our VPC for hosted POC.
10:23 Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 and KMS docs; for hosted POC logs can be redacted and we can use dedicated options for data isolation. We'll note that in the runbook.
11:00 Priya: Back to SLOs - we propose framing success criteria as: pass/fail on interactive SLO (TTFT p95/p99 thresholds), pass/fail on throughput SLO (sustained RPS and TPOT p95), and qualitative quality checks (generation quality/regression) tied to a prompt eval set.
11:35 Samir: The quality check is key - if we trade lower latency for worse output that's no good. We'll have a 100-prompt eval set for human spot-checks and automated metrics (ROUGE/BLEU-ish for summarization).
12:05 Priya: Good. Also we'll surface cost estimates for hitting the SLOs at your scale - because hitting p99 < 600ms at high RPS can require more dedicated capacity. We'll provide cost vs latency curves in the benchmark report.
12:40 Diego: For measurement plan we need an agreed experiment matrix. Priya, can you outline what you'll run?
12:55 Priya: Sure - experiment matrix (high level):
- Model family: 7B, 13B, 33B
- Scenario A: Interactive baseline (low concurrency, measure TTFT p50/p95/p99, cold & warm cache)
- Scenario B: Sustained throughput (ramp to target RPS like 10, 50, 100 depending on ACME targets, measure TPOT and p95/p99 for total response)
- Scenario C: Stress/p99 tail simulation with noisy background traffic to emulate multi-tenant contention
- Collect GPU metrics, queue latencies, kernel times, and raw request traces.
13:55 Samir: Target RPS for interactive is roughly 15 RPS sustained for peak, spikes to 60 for 30s; summarization jobs run as batch windows and need throughput of ~500 tokens/s aggregate during windows.
14:30 Jordan: we'll craft load profiles from those numbers. We'll also recommend concurrency knobs and batching settings; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization + batching configs.
15:00 Lynn: For pass/fail thresholds let's write them explicitly in the plan. Proposed by ACME earlier: interactive TTFT p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms; per-token p95 <= 60ms. Throughput: sustain 15 RPS with p95 response <= 800ms under load.
15:35 Priya: We'll test those and provide guidance. Some translation note: 800ms response at 15 RPS might be achievable with 13B in dedicated but depends on average response length; we'll include tokens-per-response assumptions.
16:00 Diego: How do you measure TPOT exactly? Is it average time per token or tail per-token?
16:12 Priya: TPOT measured as end-to-end per-token latency derived from token timestamps; we report p50/p95/p99 per-token and normalized tokens/sec. We also report TTFT as time from request receipt to first generated token. There might be tokenizer differences so we'll normalize by tokenization.
16:50 Samir: If we run the benchmarks, what's the expected turnaround for Redwood to analyze and send results?
17:00 Jordan: After the run we usually need 3-4 business days to analyze (aggregate histograms, add cost estimates). If quick triage requested we can do 24-48 hour turnaround at additional priority.
17:25 Lynn: ok. Any other blockers? We need a signed NDA before sending sensitive traces.
17:35 Jordan: Noted, we'll route NDA.
18:00 Priya: A couple subtle points from prior POCs: 1) warm-up period matters a lot for p99; include a 15-30 minute warmup run before recording metrics, 2) sampling window should be long enough to capture tail events, recommend 30m for baseline and 60m for throughput ramp tests.
19:00 Samir: Good call. Also we want to include a reproducibility section - exact model versions, quantization, kernel flags, and infra SKU.
19:25 Priya: We'll include a machine-readable run manifest and a human summary for each run.
20:00 Diego: For observability, can you export per-request traces to our Splunk?
20:06 Jordan: Yes we support logshipping and can provide a temporary S3 bucket. We'll coordinate with Lynn on access.
21:10 Lynn: ok. Can you include recommended canary thresholds for rollout if POC successful?
21:20 Priya: Yes - we'll add canary guidance: start 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with p95/p99 gating and automatic rollback on regressions.
22:05 Samir: Sounds good. Recap?
22:12 Jordan: Recap: Redwood to send benchmark plan + scripts + SOC2/KMS docs + NDA. ACME to provide prompt set and 48h traces and tokenization mapping. Run baseline week of Feb 23; Redwood to analyze results within 3-4 business days. Success criteria: TTFT p95/p99 thresholds and throughput p95 targets + quality pass.
22:45 Samir: yep that's the plan.
26:00 (cross talk, logistics about calendar invites and Slack channel)
